exposure: pregnancy-related complications (gestational hypertension, gestational diabetes, anemia, infections, preterm labor)
pharmacological treatments (antihypertensive medications, insulin therapy, iron supplementation, corticosteroids, antibiotics)
cohort: 205 pregnant women, some diagnosed with various pregnancy-related complications, observed at Navodaya Medical College Raichur, India.
finding: Patients with pregnancy-related complications required more pharmacological interventions and experienced worse outcomes, including lower gestational age at delivery, higher rates of preterm birth, more cesarean sections, and increased adverse drug reactions like hypertensive crisis and hypoglycemia.
mod_finding: Patients with pregnancy-related complications and subsequent pharmacological interventions had significantly higher rates of cesarean sections (49.2% vs. 20.0%).
gest_age: Gestational age at delivery ranged from 37.8 +/- 2.0 weeks in the complication group to 39.2 +/- 1.1 weeks in the control group.
